pr.title: Let a review list follow-ups for fix-pr to take on after the merge
pr.head: 7791813e10186ef7549fffaa4d02eaf66785b814

summary: Projector's review skill reads a pull request and lists what it finds. Until now it had three kinds of output: P1 and P2 findings, which open review threads and block the pull request, and P3 suggestions, which the review body lists and the fix-pr skill implements or defers on the open pull request. A real problem that was not the change's own, such as a bug already present at the base, could only be a suggestion, so fix-pr ended up weighing work that was not part of the pull request's argument.

This change adds a fourth kind, the follow-up. A reviewer gives it as a threads-file entry with "priority": "follow-up". project review publish lists it under a ### Follow-ups heading after the suggestions. It opens no thread and never holds a head back from clean. fix-pr leaves it alone while the pull request is open, and takes it into a follow-up pull request once the pull request merges.

• A follow-up stays owed across heads. Suggestions stand with the current head's selected reviews, including a full review an incremental verdict builds on. The new project review follow-ups reads follow-ups across all heads and removes repeats with the same file, line, and text.
  • The watch daemon counts them on merge. The fixer's MERGED line names both counts, such as the 2 suggestions its merged head lists and the follow-up its reviews list. A review that lists only follow-ups raises no REVIEW line.
  • The review marker is unchanged. Each section's count goes on a line of its own, so earlier releases still read the verdict.

cards.title: Terms
cards.html:
• Threads file: the JSON list of findings and listed items a reviewer hands to publish.
  • Listing: a kind of item a review lists in its body rather than posting as a thread. There are two: suggestions (P3) and follow-ups.
  • Count line: the projector-suggestions or projector-follow-ups comment before a section's label, recording the number of items.
  • Owed: what a merged pull request still owes its fixer.

cards.title: Review and validation
cards.html:
• Verdict: Clean review of 7791813, with no finding threads or suggestions.
  • Gate: Plugin validation, 263 hook tests, typecheck, the diff check, and the CI check job passed.
  • Focused tests: 21 tests passed for publishing, parsing, cross-head listing, and merged-event handling with a supported Python interpreter.
  • Scope: Large existing modules were inspected through changed sections and affected callers rather than read in full.

groups.title: Suggestions and follow-ups share one parser
groups.kicker: review.py's listed sections, publish, and the new follow-ups lister
intro: Before this change, review.py had a parser, a writer, a count reader, and an entry checker written for the suggestions section alone. The change moves those into functions that take a Listing, a small frozen dataclass naming the threads-file priority, the section heading, the label pattern, and the count-line pattern. SUGGESTIONS and FOLLOW_UPS are its two instances, so the two sections cannot drift apart.

publish now sorts each threads-file entry into a finding or one of the listings, and compose writes the suggestions section first and the follow-ups section after it. The new follow_ups reads the same reviews status counts, at every head, oldest first, and keeps each item once.

checks.text: Every caller of the renamed helpers moved to the new names, and nothing in src/, tests/, or the skills still names the old ones. Checked with a repository-wide search at the head.

files.note: The Listing dataclass and the parser, writer, and lister that now take one.

checks.text: Listing is frozen, so it is hashable and publish keys its entries by it.

with_counts splits the body again after inserting each count line, so the follow-ups label's index is right. The suggestions parser stops at the blank line before the follow-ups count line. Checked by reading parse_listing and by PublishFollowUpTests, which passed locally.
De-duplication keys on file, line, and text, so a repeat at a moved line lists twice. The review skill has the reviewer run project review follow-ups first and leave repeats out.

groups.title: The MERGED line counts follow-ups
groups.kicker: watch.py's Owed and the CLI command
intro: The watch daemon tells a pull request's fixer what to do when it merges. It used to count only the suggestions on the merged head. Pass.owed now also counts the follow-ups of every review, through the same follow_up_items the CLI uses, and returns an Owed pair. closing_actions names whichever counts are non-zero, and when both are zero it falls back to the old line, which asks the fixer to take any suggestion it deferred.
The CLI gains project review follow-ups, which shares its handler with suggestions, and the Codex allow rule names it.

files.note: Registers review follow-ups and routes it through the handler suggestions uses.
Adds follow-ups to the Codex allow rule for review steps.
Owed counts suggestions and follow-ups for the MERGED line.

checks.text: The reviews the daemon counts come from the paginated REST read in read_reviews, not the GraphQL last:100 query, so follow-ups from early heads count on a long pull request too.

groups.title: The skills say where a follow-up goes
intro: These files are instructions an agent follows. The review method now files a pre-existing defect, a problem in untouched code, a gap between a written rule and practice, or an improvement too large to fold in, as a follow-up instead of a P3. The test is whether the work belongs in this pull request. fix-pr builds no follow-up on the open pull request, and after the merge it lists both suggestions and follow-ups, verifies each against the base, and may split unrelated ones into separate pull requests.

files.note: Counts a follow-up still owed on a merged pull request as unfinished work.
Leaves follow-ups alone on an open pull request and takes them on after the merge.
Defines a follow-up and its threads-file entry, and narrows P3 to work that belongs in this pull request.
Files a pre-existing defect and a rule-versus-practice gap as follow-ups.

groups.title: Documentation
intro: The CLI reference documents the new command, the section format, the refusals, and the new MERGED wording. The plugin overview explains follow-ups in one paragraph.

groups.title: Tests
intro: PublishFollowUpTests checks the two sections, their count lines, the refusals, and that release 0.7.19's marker reader still reads the verdict. FollowUpListingTests checks the cross-head listing and de-duplication. Three daemon tests check the MERGED and REVIEW lines.

checks.text: Ran the publishing, listing, parser, and three follow-up watcher regressions: 21 tests passed. The configured gate also passed, including 263 hook tests and CI.
